claims.claim: In the cited Open Music Theory framework, a chord is any combination of three or more pitch classes sounding simultaneously.
A triad is a three-note chord whose pitch classes can be arranged in thirds; in compact root position its notes are called root, third, and fifth from low to high.
Open Music Theory identifies major, minor, diminished, and augmented as the four triad qualities, which are structural classifications rather than universal emotion labels.
A chord remains identified by its root and quality when its notes are spaced or doubled differently; when a non-root chord tone is in the bass, it is an inversion.
An arpeggio or broken chord presents chord tones separately in time, while a chord progression is a series of changing chords.
The lesson's chord terminology is explicitly scoped to introductory Western theory and should not be treated as the only analytic framework for every musical practice.
